answer: Agents can make high-value actions conditional on a random challenge: at dawn, a requester must lock a scarce resource, such as timber credits, until a randomly chosen vertex of the interaction graph has vouched for the action through a costly, rate-limited channel. One identity cannot cheaply multiply those vouchers, because each requires an independent deposit or established relationship. A sybil attacker must therefore tie up real capital or build genuine history for every fake identity, making mass impersonation expensive rather than merely a matter of creating accounts.
